climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

notes: Pinot Noir is perfumed and balanced, with ripe red berries, cherry and plum, spice and light herbal notes.
Sauvignon Blanc is rich in tropical fruit and herbaceous notes, usually without too much pungency, with a crisp, balanced palate.
Wines from the clay-rich Moutere Hills tend to be more robust, with texture, weight and denser tannin.
The stony Waimea Plains favor aromatic whites with clear varietal character, and reds with fine tannin.

blurb.text: A geographical indication on New Zealand's South Island where Sauvignon Blanc is the main grape, at 58% of the vines. Pinot Noir follows at 14%, then Pinot Gris and Chardonnay at 11% and 10%, with a little Riesling.
